prerequisites: Rudiments of the differential and integral calculus.

learning_outcomes.text: To make students acquainted with basic notions, methods and progresses of probability theory, descriptive statistics and mathematical statistics.
To develop students' stochastic way of thinking for modelling real phenomena and processes in engineering branches.

To obtain the needed knowledge of the probability theory, descriptive statistics and mathematical statistics, which will enable them to understand and apply stochastic models of technical phenomena based upon these methods.

syllabus_topics: Random events, probability, conditional probability, independent events.
Random variable, functional characteristics.
Numerical characteristics of random variables. Introduction to basic distributions.
Basic distributions – continuation (properties and application).
Random vector, types, functional and numerical characteristics.
Random sample, sample characteristics (properties, sample from N).
Parameters estimation (point and interval estimates of parameters N and Bi).
Testing statistical hypotheses (types, basic concepts) – one-sample tests.
Testing statistical hypotheses – two-sample tests.
Testing statistical hypotheses – multi-sample tests, goodness of fit tests.
Elements of regression analysis. – introduction, point estimates
Regression analysis – interval estimates, hypotheses testing.
Regression analysis – diagnostics, other regression models, Summary of covered topics.
Descriptive statistics (one-dimensional sample).
Descriptive statistics (two-dimensional sample). Combinatorics. Semester work assignment.
Probability, conditional probability, independent events.
System reliability, random variables – functional and numerical characteristics.
Random variables – continuation.
Basic probability distributions (Minitab – reliability diagrams).
Two-dimensional discrete random vector, functional and numerical characteristics. CLT illustration
Written exam. Interval estimates.
Testing hypotheses of one-dimensional parameters, power of tests.
Testing hypotheses of parameters in two samples.
ANOVA, chisquare tests (equality of probabilities of more categories), goodness of fit tests.
Regression analysis – regression line.
Regression analysis – model, assignment submission.
Computer seminars follow up the topics covered in seminars using statistical software (Excel, Minitab).
assessment_rules: Seminar credit conditions include active attendance in practices, sufficient or better on the written exam, and admission of the semester assignment. The examination consists of a practical part (0-80 points) and a theoretical part (4 tasks, 0-5 points each). Evaluation is based on the total number of points from both parts: excellent (90–100 points), very good (80–89 points), good (70–79 points), satisfactory (60–69 points), sufficient (50–59 points), failed (0–49 points). Attendance at seminars is controlled, and compensation for absences is at the teacher's discretion.
